clue.text: Still organising heist with two teams

indicators.note: organising a set of letters means putting them into a new order, so the heist letters are rearranged

parts.note: the word heist used letter for letter as anagram fodder
two copies of the word team, written out side by side

explanation.surface: A gang plans a robbery using two crews working in parallel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Still' looks like an adverb about the gang, but it is the definition in its 'nevertheless' sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Still and the phrase both mean nevertheless or even so, a concession made in an argument.

clue.text: Lean on King and Queen, mind

parts.note: lean as an adjective means slim, without fat
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the regnal abbreviation for the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone is advised to lean on royalty when deciding what to think.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Lean on' reads as relying on someone; 'on' is only a joining word placing the royal letters after the slim word.
explanation.definitionFit: A great mind is a person of intellect, an intellectual who reasons deeply.

clue.text: Strip show permitted inadvertent stroke?

indicators.note: stripping a word peels away its outside letters, leaving the inner pair of show

parts.note: the word show, whose outer letters are stripped off
OK means allowed or approved

explanation.surface: A striptease was licensed, though something went accidentally wrong.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Strip show' looks like a striptease; 'Strip' is an instruction to remove the outer letters of 'show'.
explanation.definitionFit: In golf or cricket this is a shot that curves away unintentionally, an errant stroke; the question mark flags it as one example.

clue.text: Second series following child in squalid part of town

indicators.note: following tells us the series word comes after the child word

parts.note: a kid is a young child
a row is a line or series of things

explanation.surface: A second run of misfortune hits a youngster in a rough district.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase names a run-down urban area of cheap lodgings and down-and-outs.

clue.text: Initially, maybe Ayrton Senna's gutted about car — this might make a flutter more attractive?

definitions.text: this might make a flutter more attractive?

indicators.note: initially picks out the opening letter of each of the words maybe and Ayrton

parts.note: the two words whose first letters are taken

indicators.note: about means the outer letters go around the word car
gutting a word removes its insides, keeping only the first and last letters of Senna

parts.note: the name Senna; the 's is just 'is'
taken as written

explanation.surface: The racing driver Ayrton Senna is devastated by something to do with his car.
explanation.walkthrough: The motor-racing picture of a flutter (a bet) misleads: the flutter is of eyelashes.
explanation.definitionFit: This cosmetic darkens eyelashes, so batting them in a flirtatious flutter looks more alluring.

clue.text: Possibly saw Rob in retirement

indicators.note: retiring means going back, so the word is read backwards

parts.note: to loot is to rob or plunder

explanation.surface: A man called Rob may have seen something after he retired.
explanation.walkthrough: 'saw' looks like the past of see and Rob like a name; saw is a noun and rob a verb.
explanation.definitionFit: A saw is one example of an implement, hence 'Possibly' marking it as an instance of the category.

clue.text: Spoil 11 across — at last Mike reveals political ideology

parts.note: to mar is to spoil or damage
XI is eleven in Roman numerals

indicators.note: at last takes the final letter of the word across

parts.note: the word across, whose final letter is taken
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Something ruins the cleaner, and finally a man called Mike reveals his politics.
explanation.walkthrough: '11 across' points at another clue in the grid, but here the number is read as a Roman numeral and 'across' as a separate word.
explanation.definitionFit: The communist theory of Karl Marx is a political and economic doctrine.

clue.text: Paper having new article on first to invest in protective clothing business planned

parts.note: the i is a British daily newspaper
the is the definite article

indicators.note: in places that letter inside the protective clothing

parts.note: PPE is personal protective equipment

indicators.note: first to takes the opening letter of invest

parts.note: the word invest, whose first letter is taken
a line of business is one's trade

explanation.surface: A newspaper runs a fresh piece about early investment in a firm making protective gear.
explanation.walkthrough: 'business planned' reads as one phrase, but business is the last piece and planned alone is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something being prepared or scheduled but not yet arrived is said to be on its way in this idiom.

clue.text: Ignore following switch — it's a perk of the job

indicators.note: following says the ignore word comes after the switch word

parts.note: to trade is to swap or exchange
to discount something is to disregard it

explanation.surface: An instruction to disregard what comes next, followed by remarks on a job benefit.
explanation.walkthrough: 'it's' is a joining word before the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A reduced price given to people in the same industry is a benefit that comes with working in that business.

clue.text: Bishop replacing foremost of vicars in revolutionary West African capital

indicators.note: revolutionary means turned round, so the word is read backwards
replacing tells us one letter is swapped for another

parts.note: an Ivorian is a person from Côte d'Ivoire (Ivory Coast)

indicators.note: foremost of takes the opening letter of vicars

parts.note: the word vicars, whose first letter is the one replaced

explanation.surface: A bishop takes the place of the leading vicar in a rebel West African church.
explanation.definitionFit: Nairobi is the capital city of Kenya, a seat of national government in East Africa.

clue.text: Safer to retain company cleaner

indicators.note: to retain means the first word holds the other inside it

parts.note: surer means more certain, more secure

explanation.surface: It is safer to keep the firm's cleaner on the payroll.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cleaner' looks like a person employed by the company; it is a scrubbing pad.
explanation.definitionFit: A scourer is a pad used for scrubbing pans, one kind of cleaning implement.

clue.text: Tramp hiding in Greenwich Ikea

indicators.note: hiding in signals the answer is concealed within the following words

parts.note: the run of letters spanning the end of Greenwich and the start of Ikea

explanation.surface: A vagrant is lurking inside the Ikea store in Greenwich.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Tramp' looks like a vagrant (noun); it is the verb meaning to walk a long way. Greenwich is a district of London.
explanation.definitionFit: To tramp is to walk a long distance, the same as going on a long walk.

clue.text: Kingmaker hands title out one's accepted — I thought that too!

indicators.note: one is accepted, that is taken into the scrambled letters
the words are put out of their order and rearranged

parts.note: one is I, the Roman numeral; the 's is read as is

explanation.surface: A kingmaker hands out a title, accepted by someone who agrees with the decision.
explanation.walkthrough: Rearrange the nineteen letters of KINGMAKER HANDS TITLE and add I for one to make twenty. Kingmaker suggests Warwick, but no history is needed.
explanation.definitionFit: Great minds think alike is the jokey phrase said when someone has the same idea as you.

clue.text: Time as member of parliament for example

definitions.meaning: second meaning: a parliament is the collective noun for owls or rooks, so one member is a feathered creature

explanation.surface: How long a person serves as a member of parliament, for example.
explanation.walkthrough: 'member of parliament' points at an MP, but the parliament is a group of rooks or owls.
explanation.definitionFit: Bird is rhyming slang (bird lime, time) for a prison term, and also any feathered animal.

clue.text: See 13
See 13
Turn up and compete week after opening of rifle range

indicators.note: after puts the compete and week letters after the opening of rifle
turning a word round reverses it, here the word up

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: opening of takes the first letter of rifle

parts.note: the word rifle, whose first letter is taken
to vie is to compete

explanation.surface: Someone shows up to compete at a rifle range for a week.
explanation.walkthrough: 'range' looks like the firing range of the surface; it means scope.
explanation.definitionFit: A purview is the scope of something's authority or concern, the extent it covers.

clue.text: Embarrassed a fake journalist

parts.note: taken as written
a sham is a fake or fraud
ED, short for editor, is the usual crossword journalist

explanation.surface: A reporter is mortified at being exposed as a fraud.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words describe feeling shame or self-conscious discomfort about something done.

clue.text: Conservative pursuing job with party as researcher?

indicators.note: pursuing means following behind, so the Conservative letter goes at the end

parts.note: a post is a job or position
a do is a party or celebration

explanation.surface: A Tory chases a job with a political party as a researcher.
explanation.walkthrough: 'party' suggests a political party, but it is a social do.
explanation.definitionFit: A postdoctoral fellow is an academic doing research after a doctorate; the question mark notes not all researchers are one.

clue.text: Challenge villain caught chasing good person

parts.note: ST, for saint, is the usual good person

indicators.note: caught here means heard, so the villain word is given by its sound

parts.note: a wretch is a despicable person

explanation.surface: A dare: the crook is nabbed while chasing a saint.
explanation.walkthrough: 'caught' looks like an arrest, but it means caught by the ear: wretch and retch sound alike because the W is silent.
explanation.definitionFit: A stretch is something that tests one's ability, a demanding task.

clue.text: Some men go loco over perfume

indicators.note: over means turned over, so the run is read backwards
some of the words means a run of letters taken from inside them

parts.note: the letters run on across these words, read from the end backwards

explanation.surface: A few men go crazy for a scent.
explanation.definitionFit: Eau de cologne is a light scented water, a kind of fragrance.

clue.text: Starts to take stock after mostly hating cycling helmets

indicators.note: after puts those opening letters behind the rest
cycling moves letters round from front to back
mostly means all but the last letter of hating

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: starts to takes the opening letter of each of take and stock

parts.note: the two words whose first letters are taken

explanation.surface: A cyclist who hates helmets has to take stock of them.
explanation.walkthrough: 'cycling helmets' looks like bike gear; 'cycling' is the instruction to rotate letters. Tin hats are military steel helmets.
explanation.definitionFit: A tin hat is a soldier's steel helmet, so the plural is a set of protective headgear.

clue.text: Leave shed

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to depart, as a plane leaves the ground
second meaning: to remove clothing, as in taking a coat off

explanation.definitionFit: The phrasal verb means both to depart suddenly and to remove a garment.

clue.text: Fed story back to their studio

parts.note: ate means fed, consumed food
a lie is a story, a fib

indicators.note: back to takes the last letter of their

parts.note: the word their, whose last letter is taken

explanation.surface: A tall tale is fed back to the people who own a studio.
explanation.walkthrough: 'back' looks like it reverses something; it only picks the final letter.
explanation.definitionFit: An atelier is an artist's or designer's workshop, a workroom for creative work.

clue.text: Learning new role

indicators.note: new signals the letters of role are made into a new arrangement

parts.note: the word role used letter for letter as anagram fodder

explanation.definitionFit: Lore is traditional knowledge, the body of wisdom passed down through study.

clue.text: See 13
Leading man, 29 making variable husband

indicators.note: making the variable a husband means swapping one letter for another

parts.note: the answer to 29 across means love or nil, which is another word for nought
Z is a standard algebraic variable

explanation.surface: A leading actor turns a nobody into a fickle husband.
explanation.walkthrough: 'variable husband' reads as a fickle spouse, but it means turning the variable letter into the husband letter.
explanation.definitionFit: The hero is the principal male character in a story, the protagonist.

clue.text: Wrong to assume good character

indicators.note: to assume means to take on, so the wrong word takes in the good letter

parts.note: a sin is a wrong or moral offence

explanation.surface: It is a mistake to suppose a person has a good nature.
explanation.walkthrough: 'character' looks like moral nature, but it means a written symbol.
explanation.definitionFit: A sign is a symbol such as a plus or a letter, which is what a typographic character is.

clue.text: Function of 27 by the sound of it

indicators.note: this phrase tells us to take a word that is pronounced like the answer to 27

parts.note: the answer to 27 down, a symbol

explanation.surface: A query about what job the 27 does, judged by its sound.
explanation.definitionFit: Sine is a trigonometric ratio, one of the basic mathematical functions of an angle.

clue.text: Love Hearts cutting out sugar essentially

indicators.note: cutting means the hearts letter slices into the out phrase

parts.note: out means not in
H is the card-suit abbreviation for hearts

indicators.note: essentially takes the central letter of sugar

parts.note: the word sugar, whose central letter is taken

explanation.surface: Someone gives up Love Hearts, the British fizzy sweets, to cut out sugar.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Love Hearts' reads as the name of the sweets, but Love is the definition alone.
explanation.definitionFit: Love is the tennis score for no points, a zero score.

clue.text: Feeling round cog

parts.note: O is round in shape
a pinion is a small cogwheel

explanation.surface: Sensing one's way around a gear wheel.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Feeling' looks like an emotion or touching; it means a view held.
explanation.definitionFit: A feeling about something is a belief or view, a personal judgement.

clue.text: Clue for hater to see different attitude

definitions.meaning: read as an instruction, the phrase works as a clue: rearranging the letters of heart gives hater
the plain sense: a reversal of one's opinion

explanation.surface: A clue for someone who hates is a chance to see things anew.
explanation.walkthrough: This is a reverse clue: the answer phrase, read as wordplay, tells you to rearrange the five-letter organ word, which spells the clue's 'hater'.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means a reversal of mind, a new opinion replacing the old.
